text:
alex: Heads-up — ran two quick Nsight captures to debug weird kernel selection & KV evictions during high-concurrency batching. Passive sampling (short duration) missed a context switch that triggers fallback kernels; active probe run exposed a burst of tiny kernels that appear to cause KV-cache thrash. Details below. :thinking:

maría: can you paste the exact commands you ran?

alex: Sure — passive short capture:
```
nsys profile --output=passive_short --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample-freq=1000 --duration=5s --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx -- my_inference_binary --config=small.yml
```
I then did a probe-style run with warmup + bracket: 
```
nsys profile --output=probe_bracket --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample-freq=2000 --duration=40s --capture-range=process:pid=12345 --osrt-range=warmup,steady -- my_inference_binary --config=small.yml
```
passive_short was ~4MB; probe_bracket ~86MB.

jon: interesting — did you use `--sample-freq` as wall-clock or hw counter? we typically set 1000 for quick checks but it can alias short-lived kernels.

alex: it's sample-freq in hz (events per sec). With a 5s capture the sample window just didn't catch the micro kernels (~50-200us) that are doing the KV handoff. The probe run with continuous sampling + longer duration shows repeating tiny kernels on CUDA stream 7 at ~3-6k/s during canary batches.

sophia: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? NVTX markers around batching would help isolate start/end of prefix/decoder and the decision point for kernel choice.

alex: pasted a trimmed timeline (nvtx colors preserved):
```
[...timeline excerpt...]
13.4ms kernel: prep_batch_kernel (small)
0.18ms kernel: k_cache_handoff (tiny)
0.32ms kernel: attention_fwd_small (tiny)
15.0ms kernel: decoder_block
(kv-evict spikes right after k_cache_handoff x12)
```
Noticed that when the runtime picks an "optimized" kernel for long sequences it misses a fast-path for small sequences; the fallback path does an extra memcpy which triggers KV eviction thrash.

maría: could be batching heuristic: sequenced inputs cause frequent small KV writes at tail. Did you try forcing kernel selection via env var (e.g., RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=fast_small)?

alex: tried `RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=fast_small` — removed the tiny-kernel storm and reduced evictions by ~70% in the probe trace. But latency for long sequences regressed slightly (2.1ms -> 2.7ms). So it's a tradeoff.

jon: maybe a dynamic heuristic: sample the seq-length distribution and pick per-batch kernel. We should add NVTX around the decision point to correlate decisions with KV churn.

sophia: also try increasing `--osrt-sample-window` beyond the default, and use `--capture-sample-thread` to reduce noise. For CI we could adopt a short bracketed probe: 10s warmup + 30s steady.

perf-bot: nsys artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/probe_bracket_1718201234.qdmp (size 86MB) :white_check_mark:

alex: next steps: 1) add NVTX markers before/after batching and KV ops; 2) run probe bracket with RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL toggles; 3) compare kernel timelines and KV eviction counts (perf counters). Will post diffs. Thanks y'all :rocket:
